claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC alloy.
Equiatomic disordered-BCC NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The high Mo content of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is associated with reduced plasticity.
Cold rolling followed by a 600–650°C sub-recrystallization anneal can induce a nano-twinned, uniformly recovered microstructure in equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
Cold rolling introduces a high density of dislocations and other defect structures.
A sub-recrystallization anneal reorganizes the cold-rolling defects into nano-twins and partially recovered regions.
The treatment reduces local strain heterogeneities.
Nano-twins and partially recovered regions improve plasticity by enabling controlled dislocation motion.
Grain-boundary strengthening and dislocation pinning preserve high strength after the treatment.
The proposed microstructural features compensate for the embrittling effects associated with high Mo content.
After treatment, room-temperature compressive yield strength will remain within approximately 10% of the 1719 MPa baseline.
After treatment, plastic strain before failure will increase by approximately 20% relative to the untreated alloy.
The strength–plasticity improvement requires sufficient pre-anneal cold deformation.
Complete recrystallization or secondary-phase precipitation would prevent the proposed strength–plasticity balance.
Annealing outside 600–650°C may fail to produce the proposed strength–plasticity improvement.
Controlled cooling will retain the modified microstructure.
